technical.summary: Extreme oversold bounce signals (RSI 16, Stoch 5) with bullish divergence are offset by pervasive bearish structure (price below all MAs, MACD negative, Ichimoku below cloud), making this a potential mean-reversion trap rather than high-probability swing entry.

fundamental.summary: AEP shows no insider buying conviction, no institutional accumulation signal, zero government contract activity, no lobbying engagement, and minimal retail interest; earnings in 24 days present elevated risk with no offsetting fundamental or smart money support.

sentiment.summary: Extreme fear (VIX-equivalent 17) presents contrarian buy opportunity, but congressional activity is stale (291+ days old) with only small sales, and absent news sentiment limits conviction.

risk.summary: Severe macro headwinds: inverted yield curve signals recession risk, VIX at crisis levels (322.4) indicates extreme market stress, strong dollar pressures multinationals, and earnings in 24 days adds event risk to utilities sector already facing credit stress.

debate.key_bull_argument: Extreme RSI oversold (16) with stochastic bullish cross and volume spike divergence create textbook mean-reversion setup at support (74.557), offering asymmetric risk/reward if bounce initiates.
debate.key_bear_argument: Pervasive bearish structure (price below all MAs, MACD negative, Ichimoku below thick cloud resistance) combined with severe macro headwinds (inverted yield curve, VIX crisis, earnings event risk in 24 days) and zero fundamental/smart money support make this a classic oversold trap rather than high-probability entry.
